surfaceMeaning: Standard grid on a source-informed shape model; no resolved global surface map.
name: Varda
credit: Proudfoot et al. (2026), occult3d reanalysis of Souami et al. (2020) occultation chords
shapeMeaning: One published allowable triaxial model, with semiaxes 389, 353 and 248 km. The line-of-sight depth is unconstrained; these best-fit values illustrate a solution rather than a uniquely measured body shape.
orientationMeaning: Assumes the spin pole aligns with Ilmarë’s orbit: J2000 RA 272.6° and declination −10.8°. This is a model prior; rotational phase and meridian are illustrative.
periodText: Unresolved; photometric aliases and synchronous rotation remain alternatives
introduction: Varda is a distant binary-system primary whose outline was measured as it eclipsed a star. Its companion’s orbit helps orient this model, but Varda’s depth remains uncertain.

numericEvidence.section: Proudfoot et al. (2026), Table 1, Table 3, Figure 4 and section 5.2
numericEvidence.axisUncertaintyMeaning: The paper intentionally reports only an example best fit for Varda: c/a is unconstrained. No axis confidence interval or precise physical volume is asserted.
numericEvidence.radiusFormula: cbrt(389 * 353 * 248); volume-equivalent radius of this displayed model only
numericEvidence.poleMeaning: J2000 equatorial orbit-pole prior, not an independently observed surface pole

unresolved: Depth and volume are not uniquely measured; many c/a values remain possible.
Spin-orbit alignment is assumed, and no absolute phase or sidereal period is installed.
Additional 2018 occultation chords mentioned in conference proceedings were not publicly released in the 2026 analysis.

sourceSurvey.provides: Updated satellite orbit and a triaxial example model
sourceSurvey.reason: Most recent qualified numeric fit found; explicit depth degeneracy is retained.

sourceSurvey.provides: Five measured occultation chords and several Maclaurin interpretations
sourceSurvey.reason: The 2026 study rules out the older mirror-orbit interpretation supporting the spheroidal fit if spin and satellite orbit are aligned.
These are unresolved time-series measurements; no spatial surface mosaic or additional terrain is implied.
